title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Marina Lopez
description:
Motivation: The continuous batcher scheduler was observed to favor high-throughput request classes leading to starvation of low-rate, latency-sensitive requests in mixed workloads. This change tunes queueing, fairness weights, and adds starvation prevention/timeouts to ensure latency SLOs for latency-sensitive routes while preserving batching efficiency for throughput routes.

Design summary: Introduce a multi-queue scheduler with weighted deficit-based fairness and per-queue starvation detectors. New knobs: per-queue target_latency_ms, max_queue_time_ms (hard timeout), fairness_weight, and a starvation_boost window where starving queues receive temporary scheduling priority. We also add a global max_batch_wait_ms guard to avoid unbounded aggregation for very low-rate queues. The scheduler uses a compact token-bucket to track credit and a lightweight latency histogram for per-queue tail estimates.

Implementation details: - scheduler: implement WeightedDeficitScheduler in src/serving/continuous_batcher/scheduler.rs with O(1) enqueue/dequeue for active queues - queue metadata: add target_latency_ms, fairness_weight, starvation_timer to queue struct - timeouts: per-request enqueue timestamp used to trigger starvation_boost and max_queue_time_ms enforcement - metrics: new metrics batcher.queue_starvation_count, batcher.queue_max_queue_time, batcher.fairness_imbalance_ratio - config: extend configs/batcher_config.yaml with new knobs and defaults tuned from lab experiments - tests: unit tests for fairness invariants and e2e benchmark harness for mixed workload (small/large requests)

review_comments: Evan Park: Can we make the starvation_boost window configurable? In some clusters the default 50ms felt aggressive.
Marina Lopez: responded - made starvation_boost window configurable via starvation_boost_ms and added a note about safe defaults (50ms for mixed workloads).
Priya Nair: Please add a small microbenchmark that exercises low-rate 1-token requests to validate the max_batch_wait_ms guard.
Marina Lopez: added perf canary job and included test harness in tests/continuous_batcher/test_fairness.rs
Samir Gupta: LGTm after addressing timeout edge case where queue_time could overflow an int64 on extremely long-running enqueues.
CI: initial run failed - flaky test test_fairness::starvation_detector timing; fixed by replacing wall-clock sleeps with simulated timers
release_notes: Improved continuous batcher scheduler: weighted fairness, starvation prevention, per-queue timeouts, and several new telemetry metrics. Default behavior preserved; feature gated behind continuous_batcher.fairness_v2.
notes: Rollout plan: enable in canary region for 48 hours and monitor batcher.queue_starvation_count and route-level latency SLOs before global rollout. If fairness_imbalance_ratio > 1.2 or tail latencies regress, rollback the feature flag and revert to previous scheduler.
benchmarks_summary: Mixed workload: latency-sensitive median 120ms->35ms, p99 520ms->85ms; throughput impact <3%; scheduler CPU ~+1.8% per-core.
docs_updates: Added config docs and metrics doc for observability; updated best-practices in docs/observability/metrics.md.
